<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par52 />passives of Qal. He reckons as such all those ''perfects'', of which the {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} (which ought to express the corresponding active) is either not found at all, or only (as in the case of {{GHGheb|text=יִלֵּד}}) with a different meaning, and which form their {{GHGterm|imperfect}} from another conjugation, generally Niphʿal. Such ''perfects'' are the ''quṭṭal'' form of the stems {{GHGheb|text=אבל}} ({{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=תְּאֻבְּלוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=20}}), {{GHGheb|text=חפשׁ}}, {{GHGheb|text=טרף}}, {{GHGheb|text=ילד}}, {{GHGheb|text=יצר}}, {{GHGheb|text=לקח}}, {{GHGheb|text=עבד}}, {{GHGheb|text=שׁגל}}, {{GHGheb|text=שׁטף}}, {{GHGheb|text=שׁפךְ}}. Barth (see below) adds to the list the apparent {{GHGterm|Puʿal}}-''perfects'' of {{GHGheb|text=אסר}}, {{GHGheb|text=בזז}}, {{GHGheb|text=זנה}}, {{GHGheb|text=חצב}}, {{GHGheb|text=כרת}}, {{GHGheb|text=נפח}}, {{GHGheb|text=עזב}}, {{GHGheb|text=עשה}}, {{GHGheb|text=ראה}}, and of verbs with middle {{GHGheb|text=ר}} (hence with ''ŭ'' of the first syllable lengthened to ''ō''), {{GHGheb|text=הרג}}, {{GHGheb|text=הרה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=3|verse=3}} [{{GHGheb|text=זרה}}, see {{GHGpar|67|m}}], {{GHGheb|text=זרע}}, {{GHGheb|text=זרק}}, {{GHGheb|text=טרף}}, {{GHGheb|text=מרט}}, {{GHGheb|text=קרא}}, {{GHGheb|text=שׂרף}}; also the infinitives absolute {{GHGheb|text=הֹרוֹ וְהֹגוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=59|verse=13}}. In these cases there is no need to assume any error on the part of the punctuators; the sharpening of the second radical may have taken place in order to retain the characteristic ''ŭ'' of the first syllable (cf. Arab. ''qŭtĭlă'' as passive of ''qătălă''), and the ''a'' of the second syllable is in accordance with the vocalization of all the other passives (see {{GHGpar|39|f}}). Cf. {{GHGpar|52|s}} and {{GHGpar|53|u}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|f}}
'''2.''' The fundamental idea of {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, to which all the various shades of meaning in this conjugation may be referred, is to ''busy oneself eagerly'' with the action indicated by the stem. This intensifying of the idea of the stem, which is outwardly expressed by the strengthening of the second radical, appears in individual cases as—(''a'') a ''strengthening'' and ''repetition'' of the action (cf. the ''intensive'' and ''iterative'' nouns with the middle radical strengthened, {{GHGpar|84||b}}),<ref>Analogous examples, in which the strengthening of a letter has likewise an ''intensive'' force, are such German words as ''reichen, recken'' (Eng. ''to reach, to rack''); ''streichen'' (''stringo''), ''strecken'': cf. ''Strich'' (''a stroke''), ''Strecke'' (''a stretch''); ''wacker'' from ''wachen''; others, in which it has the ''causative'' sense, are ''stechen, stecken''; ''wachen'' (''watch''), ''wecken'' (''wake''); τέλλω ''to bring to an end'' (cf. the stem τέλω ''to end'', in τέλος, τελέω); γεννάω ''to beget'', from the stem γένω ''to come into being'' (cf. γένος).</ref> e.g. {{GHGheb|text=צָחַק|translate=to laugh}}, Piʿēl ''to jest, to make sport'' (to laugh repeatedly); {{GHGheb|text=שָׁאַל|translate=to ask}}, Piʿēl ''to beg''; hence when an action has reference to ''many'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=קָבַר|translate=to bury}} (a person) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=23|verse=4}}, Piʿēl ''to bury'' (many) {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=11|verse=15}}, and often so in Syr. and Arab. Other varieties of the ''intensive'' and ''iterative'' meaning are, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=פָּתַח|translate=to open}}, Piʿēl ''to loose''; {{GHGheb|text=סָפַר|translate=to count}}, Piʿēl ''to recount'': [cf. {{GHGheb|text=כִּתֵּב}}, {{GHGheb|text=חִשֵּׁב}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִלֵּךְ}}, {{GHGheb|text=רִפֵּא}}, {{GHGheb|text=חִפֵּשׂ}}, {{GHGheb|text=תִּפֵּשׂ}}; {{GHGheb|text=מְאַהֵב}}, {{GHGheb|text=מְרַצֵּחַ}}].

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|g}}
The eager pursuit of an action may also consist in ''urging'' and ''causing'' others to do the same. Hence {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} has also—(''b'') a ''causative'' sense (like {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=לָמַד|translate=to learn}}, Piʿēl ''to teach''. It may often be turned by such phrases as ''to permit to, to declare'' or ''hold as'' (''the declarative Piʿēl''), ''to help to'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=חִיָּה|translate=to cause to live}}, {{GHGheb|text=צִדֵּק|translate=to declare innocent}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִלֵּד|translate=to help in child-bearing}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|h}}
(''c'') ''Denominatives'' (see {{GHGpar|38|b}}) are frequently formed in this conjugation, and generally express a being occupied with the object expressed by the noun, either to form or to make use of it, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=קִנֵּן|translate=to make a nest, to nest}} (from {{GHGheb|text=קֵן}}), {{GHGheb|text=עִפֵּר|translate=to throw dust, to dust}} (from {{GHGheb|text=עָפָר}}),<section end=par52 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
